$comment: ONE assistant message, carried across every hop that touches its identity.
The message holds TWO content blocks — a thinking block at API index 0 and a
text block at API index 1 — because that is the shape the whole class of
identity bugs hides in. A single-block message reconciles even when the two
sides disagree about what a block index means, so it proves nothing.
Reasoning is its OWN emission on the frontend surface (AgentThinking) and
is stripped from the response body, so the thinking record below curates to
an `agent.thinking` item under a derived uuid while the text record curates
to `agent.response`. Both halves of that rule are load bearing: without the
strip a renderer draws the reasoning twice, and without the emission it has
to reach into a durable message's content array to find the grey block.
Because the emission is detached from the message it came out of, it also
STATES where it came from: `apiMessageId` + `blockIndex` name the message
and the pre-strip position, which is the same pair a live preview is keyed
on. Without them the settled reasoning block cannot find its own preview and
renders beside it — the third item this fixture's expectations forbid.
Note what the SDK does with `content`: it emits ONE assistant record PER
BLOCK, both repeating `msg_01ABC` and each carrying a `content` array of
length one. So a record's own content index is always 0 and identifies
nothing, while the live deltas number the blocks 0 and 1. Any hop that
re-derives identity from the wrong one of those two ordinals reproduces the
bug this fixture exists to catch.
Consumed by:
agent-shim/claude/shim/test/stream-contract.test.ts  (sdkMessages -> wire)
daemon/internal/frontend/stream_contract_test.go     (wire -> frames)
webapp/test/stream-contract.test.ts                  (frames -> store)
Each hop asserts against the SAME fixture, so drift at any one of them fails
in CI instead of rendering twice on screen.
